svg.font-family: Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Polaris Query Execution Internals: Compilation, Scheduling, Caching, Fault Tolerance
svg.desc: An internals diagram with four decision points chained together. First, the two-phase Cascades optimizer decides per join whether to fuse it into the current task or insert a blocking data-move enforcer, based on whether inputs are already hash-aligned. Second, the resulting task DAG joins a global workload graph, where the scheduler picks FIFO under load or best-fit placement when idle capacity exists. Third, task placement is cache-affinitized to nodes, and a warning node describes the three different cache outcomes when the topology scales out, scales in, or a node fails. Fourth, a hierarchical state machine governs each task's execution, retrying transient failures at task granularity and escalating to the parent query only when a task cannot recover.
svg.text: Task-DAG compilation · scheduling decisions · cache-affinity outcomes · task-level fault tolerance
1 · TASK-DAG COMPILATION — HOW A QUERY BECOMES A DAG OF TASKS
runs natively on SQL Server node
2 · SCHEDULING DECISIONS — WORKLOAD GRAPH AT TASK-DISPATCH TIME
Union of every active query's task DAG
resource bins the scheduler packs into
heavy tasks may defer to avoid
Resource pressure on the graph triggers
not built for sub-second distributed queries
3 · CACHE-AFFINITIZED PLACEMENT — OUTCOME BY TOPOLOGY EVENT
Same data cells are consistently assigned to the same nodes, so buffer-pool / local-SSD cache state survives most topology changes.
All existing nodes keep their cached cells;
only the new node(s) start cold and warm up
Only the caches of the removed node(s) are lost;
surviving nodes' cached cells are untouched
Compute returned to region once pressure subsides
Cache on the unhealthy node is lost, but cells can be
rebuilt lazily from OneLake — never a source of truth
Operations redistributed to healthy nodes, not failed
4 · TASK-LEVEL FAULT TOLERANCE — HIERARCHICAL STATE MACHINES
Query DAG → Task Templates → Tasks, each its own state machine; failures retry at the lowest level first and escalate only when not retriable.
retriable → task redistributed to healthy node, retried at TASK granularity (query is not restarted)
only if failure is NOT retriable —
Every state transition across all three FSM levels is logged — giving reproducibility and letting a query resume execution rather than restart from scratch.
Why this shape: the two Polaris design goals
Converge data-warehouse and big-data workloads onto one engine, and fully separate compute from durable state.
Task-level scheduling, enforcer-defined boundaries, cache affinity, and FSM-driven retry are the mechanisms that jointly deliver those two goals —
not independent features. See polaris-engine.svg for how these internals sit inside the full front-end / DQP / compute / storage system.
Fuse / favorable path (no shuffle, cache warm, task succeeds)
Enforcer / scale-related event (blocking shuffle, broadcast, scale-out)
Failure / rigid constraint (node unhealthy, temp-disk cap, latency floor)
Decision point the scheduler/optimizer evaluates at runtime

g.title: Two-phase Cascades compilation — SQL Server Cascades optimizer builds the logical MEMO, then a distributed cost-based phase picks physical plans and task boundaries.

g.aria-label: Fuse task or insert data-move enforcer?
g.title: Fuse task or insert data-move enforcer? — Per join: fuse into the current task if inputs are hash-aligned, else insert a blocking enforcer.
Task DAG for the query — The compiled plan becomes a DAG of task templates whose edges encode dataflow and precedence.
Workload-graph scheduler — FIFO by default, best-fit when idle capacity exists; triggers autonomous online scale-out under pressure.
Cache affinity under topology change — Scale-out preserves existing caches; scale-in loses only removed nodes' caches; node failure redistributes tasks.
Hierarchical fault-tolerance state machine — Transient failures retry at task granularity; only non-retriable failures escalate to the parent query.
